title: fix(plugin-approvals,plugin-security): the drawer's Approve names the approved request, and Explain access names the principal as a person
body:
Fixes #23157
Clause-②: no — two server-authored strings name the record and the person; no published schema, translation key or export moves.

Two strings the console renders verbatim now name what and who they are about. This is family card #23157, rows 1 and 2, a member of objectui#12308 (classes 2 and 5).

## Row 1: the drawer's Approve toast names the approved request

`approval_approve.successMessage` in `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts` was the bare verb `Approved.`. It is now `Approved "${result.request.record_title}"`, which is the inbox row's inline Approve wording (objectui `inlineApproved`, `Approved "TITLE"`).

The zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES values of the same key now carry the same token. Each reuses objectui's own translation of `inlineApproved`. No translation key is added, and the en bundle equals the source value.

## Row 2: Explain access names the principal as a person

The principal layer in `explain-engine.ts` used to open with `Principal 1cnVm… holds position(s) …`. It now opens with `Principal Dev Admin (admin@objectos.ai; id 1cnVm…) holds position(s) …`. All three arms of the on-behalf-of delegator clause name the delegator the same way.

A new module-private helper, `personOf`, reads the user row with `ql.findOne('sys_user', …)` under the **asker's** context: the caller, or the explained principal on a self-explanation. Every data middleware applies, so the sentence names only what the asker's own read returns:

- When the read returns no row, the asker gets the bare id the sentence always carried.
- When field-level security masks a field, that field stays out.
- When the read throws or the engine has no `findOne`, the sentence falls back to the bare id.

The name is presentation only and never feeds a verdict. The decision's `principal` object is unchanged. Only the principal layer's `detail` sentence (and its delegation clause) changed. `isRlsDenySentinel` and its docblock are untouched.

**One consequence for reviewers.** Two askers can now be shown different names for the same principal, because each sees only what its own read returns. `explain-asker-gate.test.ts` compares whole decisions across askers (ruling A). Its 9 comparisons that went red on this change now go through `apartFromPrincipalPerson`, which sets aside only the person segment of the principal sentence. The record story they pin is still compared byte for byte.

## Mechanism measurements (dispatch H1 to H4)

- **H1, confirmed.** The approve route answers `svc.decide(...)` unwrapped. Measured live on a fresh showcase boot at this branch's head, `POST /api/v1/approvals/requests/ID/approve`:
  - Response keys are `decision, finalized, request, resumed, runId`, with no `data` envelope. The console's `apiHandler` therefore hands this body to the runner as `result.data`.
  - `request.record_title` was `INV-1006` on a finalizing approve and `EXP-2001` on an approve that left the step pending.
  - Filled through the runner's grammar (`${result.PATH}`, dotted path, an unresolved path becomes empty), the toast reads `Approved "INV-1006"` and `Approved "EXP-2001"`.

  So row 1 is a metadata change with no new response field. `GET /api/v1/meta/object/sys_approval_request` serves the new copy, and with zh-CN it serves `已通过“${result.request.record_title}”`.
- **H2.** All four bundles carried the value, and all four are updated in step. `check:i18n` and `check:i18n-stale-fill` are green.
- **H3.** At that point the engine holds `context.email`. For another user, though, that email comes from `resolveUserAuthzGrants`' system read, so disclosing it would widen what the asker sees. No name is in hand. So the engine reads the row through the asker's door, the engine's existing `ql` with the asker's existing context. Measured live as the admin:
  - "Me": `Principal Dev Admin (admin@objectos.ai; id 1cnVm0j9…) holds position(s) [platform_admin, …]`.
  - Explaining `usr_showcase_auditor_demo`: `Principal Ada Auditor (demo) (auditor.demo@example.com; id usr_showcase_auditor_demo) holds …`.
- **H4.** The `onBehalfOf.userId` clause is covered by the same mechanism, in its intersection, missing-delegator and unresolved arms.

## Pins

- `plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts` has a new describe block. The approve copy is filled from a real `decide()` answer, and every token must resolve. A finalizing approve gives `Approved "Acme Renewal"`. An approve that leaves a unanimous step waiting still names the record. A record whose row is gone is named from the payload snapshot.
- `plugin-approvals/src/translations/approve-success-copy-i18n.test.ts` is new. Every locale must carry the source's `${result.*}` tokens and must not echo the English source.
- `plugin-security/src/explain-principal-person.test.ts` is new and uses the real `SecurityPlugin` over a real `ObjectQL` and better-sqlite3. Each asker's own `sys_user` read is armed first: a directory admin, the principal itself, system, a field-level-security admin with email masked, and a `manage_users`-only admin whose read returns no row. Each cell then asserts the sentence the read licenses:
  - **Control:** the blind admin gets `Principal usr_pp_ada holds …`, and the whole decision contains neither the name nor the email.
  - **Control:** the masked admin gets the name and never the email.
  - **Control:** the blind and directory decisions differ only in the person.
  - The D10 cells measured the agent's intersected read and assert what it returns: both people named, only the delegator named, or neither. A delegator that does not exist is named by its id.

## Negative-pin ablations

Each ablation was committed first and run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, with an EXIT/INT/TERM trap that restores the file. Every leg proved its restore by blob hash against HEAD with an empty `git diff HEAD`. Each subject resolves through relative `src` imports, so no `dist/` leg was needed.

- **A1:** the old principal sentence, `Principal ${context?.userId ?? '(anonymous)'}` (blob `5499d10fec93` to `82a3452dbfaf`). 5 cells failed and the 7 controls held: `expected 'Principal usr_pp_ada holds position(s…' to match /^Principal Ada Lovelace \(ada@example…/`.
- **A2:** the old delegator clause in the intersection arm. 2 cells failed: `expected 'Principal Release Bot (bot@example.te…' to contain 'Acting on behalf of Grace Hopper (gra…'`.
- **B1:** the source copy back to `'Approved.'`. 7 cells failed: `expected 'Approved.' to be 'Approved "Acme Renewal"'`.
- **B2:** the zh-CN value back to `已通过。`. 1 cell failed: `zh-CN approval_approve.successMessage tokens: expected [] to deeply equal [ '${result.request.record_title}' ]`.

All four were restored with `ok restored: blob == HEAD … git diff HEAD is empty`.

## Local verification at HEAD 09218ddc1c

- **Full package suites:**
  - `@objectstack/plugin-security`: 194 files and 4008 tests passed, 45 skipped.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`: 74 files and 1042 tests passed.
- **Typecheck:** both packages' `typecheck` scripts pass. The plugin-approvals test-typecheck debt held at its ledger, and the new cells narrow the open result rather than grow the TS2339 count.
- **Derived gates:** `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 66 families from this branch's changed files. All 66 ran with exit 0, and `--ran` reconciled 66 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a derived zero).
- **Lint, narrowed:** eslint ran over the 10 changed TS files only, with 0 errors and 0 warnings. The population is eslint's own `**/*.{ts,…}` config, and the count comes from `--format json`. The narrowing excludes nothing: this config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so the diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- **Left to CI:** the type-check lanes, Test Core, Build Core and dogfood jobs.

## Acceptance notes

- **Sibling bare-verb success copies** on the same object, same family (class 2): `approval_reject` `Rejected.`, whose inline path says `Rejected "TITLE"` and whose route answers the same `decide()` result, plus `Reassigned.`, `Sent back for revision.`, `Information requested.`, `Reminder sent.`, `Recalled.`, `Resubmitted.` and `Reply posted.`. They are not changed here, because the claim's file surface names only the approve action. They would make good new rows on this family card.
- **The ADR-0091 D3 delegated-position clause** of the same principal sentence (`approver from usr_… until …`) and its contributor `via` still name a raw user id (class 5). The claim scoped this change to the principal and its on-behalf-of clause. Not reproduced live, because the showcase seeds no delegated position.
- **Residual in row 1:** a target with no resolvable title (no display-field value, and no name, title, subject or label in the snapshot) would toast `Approved ""`. The inbox's inline path falls back to the formatted record id there, and the token grammar has no fallback operator. Every request measured carried a title.
- **Cosmetic:** a display name that itself ends in parentheses reads `Ada Auditor (demo) (auditor.demo@example.com; id …)`.
- **Cost:** each explanation now makes one more `sys_user` read per person named, and one more in the nested read pass when a by-id write is explained for a row the principal cannot read.
